sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

assessment.reason: The modest model edge holds across the supplied sensitivity range, and no Copp-specific adverse listing appears in the excerpt. The edge is thin and unvalidated, and the market comparison rests on one other book.
assessment.model_case: Copp appeared on Oct 20. A projected mean of about 0.43 assists against a 0.5 line means the over needs a scoring event in a median-zero game. Ice time near 17.5 minutes drives the case. Line and power-play deployment are unverified, so the production rate could be overstated.
assessment.price_case: This is a single main 0.5 line at +250. Model fair odds are about +186 and the minimum acceptable price is about +218, so there is some cushion. The low end of the sensitivity range still clears the +250 break-even. One other book is not broad consensus.
assessment.context_case: The Detroit center absences could plausibly widen Copp's role, but nothing confirms his line or power-play usage. His absence from the table does not establish health. Vancouver's starting goalie is projected, not confirmed.

qualitative_review.countercase: The market sits close to the model, so the gap may be mostly vig rather than information. If Copp lands in a checking role without power-play time, his assist rate could fall below the shrunk estimate. The sensitivity scaling is not a confidence interval.

assessment.reason: The model case clears break-even even at the low end of the sensitivity range, but the cushion is thin. The only supplied source contains no Barbashev-specific reporting.
assessment.model_case: Barbashev played Oct 20. A projected mean of about 0.46 assists against a 0.5 line relies on roughly 16 minutes and a shrunk production rate. Unverified line placement is the main weakness: a top-six slot supports the rate, while a demotion would erode it.
assessment.price_case: This is the main 0.5 line at +210. The minimum acceptable price is about +199 and model fair odds are about +170, leaving a small margin over the +210 break-even. The market reference from one other book is near the model, so price movement of a few cents could erase the case.
assessment.context_case: The St. Louis injury list is extensive, and the Vegas absences could affect deployment, but nothing cited addresses Barbashev's role. Context is unverified and the St. Louis goalie is projected.

qualitative_review.countercase: With the model and market this close, a small overestimate of ice time or the assist rate flips the edge. Shortening the price toward +199 leaves no margin. The Hofer and Binnington goalie split is unconfirmed.

assessment.reason: At +140 the under needs only about two-in-five. The model sits above that across sensitivity, and the market roughly equals break-even. No concrete blocker is identified, but the margin is modest.
assessment.model_case: The projected mean of about three-quarters of a point and median of one show he usually produces. The under depends on the model's lower scoring estimate around 17.9 minutes. A shrunk production rate is doing meaningful work here.
assessment.price_case: Main line at +140 has a break-even near +140. Model fair is about +111. Two other books imply close to the offered price, so the market sees little value. The blended estimate shows only a slim edge.
assessment.context_case: Injury coverage for Boston is missing. A Nashville center is day-to-day, which may affect line combinations. The Kings parlay article is irrelevant. His last listed game was Oct 17, so current status is unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: He projects for close to a point on average, and the market price matches break-even. A modest underestimate of his power-play role or production erases the edge. Missing Boston injury coverage leaves opponent strength and goalie context incomplete.
